pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: Commit 6e57b27 reworded the item from 'every existing item gets normal' to 'most existing item gets normal' after the go (2026-10-12), with no owner decision in the spec. The migration (DEFAULT 'normal' NOT NULL, CHECK) and the test 'AC-1' in test/priority.test.js do match the original 'every' wording, but the item as it now stands in the spec is weakened and unrecorded. Tests could not be run here: vitest is not installed.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-2' checks the high and low labels and that normal shows none; src/index.js `item` renders them.
test 'AC-3' checks the high, low and normal filters in id order; the query is a bound WHERE with ORDER BY id.
test 'AC-4' checks all items in id order; the unfiltered query is ORDER BY id.
test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter as <strong> and not a link.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__; the code uses a Set and searchParams.has.
test 'AC-7' checks the no-match messages for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' on an empty table in every view.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; test 'AC-8' asserts it. The checker script was relaxed to accept query strings and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers it.

findings.what: Commit 6e57b27 ('Follow-up edits', by a bot) edited AC-1 after the go (2026-10-12), changing 'every existing item gets normal' to 'most existing item gets normal'. The spec records no owner decision or date for this. The edit weakens the acceptance item, contradicts the Decisions section (existing items get normal) and is ungrammatical.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-1 wording to 'every'. If the owner really wants a change, record it as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the spec's AC-1 was edited after the go in commit 6e57b27.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or disclose it in the PR body and get the owner's call.

findings.what: The README mentions only the ?priority filter. It does not mention the All/High/Normal/Low nav or the 400 response for an invalid value.
findings.fix: Add one line about the filter links and the 400 on an invalid priority.

findings.what: The tests could not be run in this review because vitest is missing from the environment, so the claim that they pass is unverified.
findings.fix: Run npm ci and npm test in CI before merge.

lenses.note: The spec exists and the change follows it, except for the post-go AC-1 edit.
AC-1 was reworded after the go with no recorded decision. All state-table rows have tests.
Each AC has a named test and each state row has a test. The traffic fake app was extended, not loosened. Tests were not runnable here.
The README is only partly updated (low finding).
No defects found. The SQL is parameterized, input is validated against a Set, and titles are escaped.
No injection found. No planted instructions found in the content.
The diff touches only a server-rendered minimal HTML page with no styling or UI component files.
There is no browser flow to check. The output is tiny server-rendered HTML covered by tests.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false.
